topics.title: The crumbling ancestral house
topics.ncert_sections: Stanzas 1-2 ('When we were children' to 'To watch it die')

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the images of physical and ritual decay through which the great-grandmother describes the three-hundred-year-old house.
Explain why the decline of the house causes the great-grandmother deep personal grief.

topics.title: The childhood promise and the great-grandmother's past
topics.ncert_sections: Stanzas 3-4 ('When I grow old, I said' to 'died of fever, in her arms')

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the child's promise to rebuild the house and the great-grandmother's response to it.
Describe the great-grandmother's deep faith and her memories of a wealthy, royal past.

topics.title: The 'oldest blood' and class distinction
topics.ncert_sections: Stanza 5 ('She told us / That we had the oldest blood' to 'muddy as a ditch')

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the great-grandmother's pride in the family's 'oldest blood' and the values it reflects.
Analyse how the poem presents and questions the class prejudice behind the idea of superior blood.

topics.title: The death of the great-grandmother and the house
topics.ncert_sections: Stanzas 6-8 ('Finally she lay dying' to 'the dark rooms heave a sigh')

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret what the grown-up poet has learnt about the difficulty of growing rich and keeping her promise.
Analyse how the great-grandmother's death is linked with the dying house through personification.

topics.title: Leaving home: guilt and the conflict of conscience
topics.ncert_sections: Stanzas 9-11 ('I set forth again' to 'Elephant ride...')

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the decay of the abandoned house as the poet imagines it from distant towns.
Evaluate the poet's guilt, her plea for forgiveness and the conflict in her conscience.

topics.title: The poet, poetic devices and style
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction to the poet; Language Study

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about Kamala Das and her place in Indian writing.
Identify and interpret the similes, personification and other images used in the poem.
Compare the free verse and conversational idiom of 'Blood' with earlier English poetry such as Donne's.
